Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১) Decreased nutrients & decreased stimulation leads to which cellular response?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Decreased nutrients and decreased stimulation lead to cellular atrophy, which is a reduction in the size of cells and often results in a decrease in the size and function of an organ. Atrophy can occur due to decreased workload, loss of innervation, diminished blood supply, inadequate nutrition, loss of endocrine stimulation, or aging. In this situation, cells adapt by reducing their metabolic activity and structural components to survive under reduced functional demands. Metaplasia is a reversible change from one differentiated cell type to another, while cellular aging and pathological calcification are different processes.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ↓ Nutrients + ↓ stimulation → Atrophy

  • Atrophy → ↓ Cell size

  • Causes → ↓ workload, denervation, ↓ blood supply, malnutrition, ↓ hormonal stimulation

  • Metaplasia → Change in differentiated cell type

  • Hypertrophy → ↑ Cell size

Exam Pearl: Decreased nutrition or stimulation → cellular atrophy.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২) Which is not ultrastructural changes in reversible cell injury?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In reversible cell injury, the major ultrastructural changes involve the plasma membrane, mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum (ER), and ribosomes. Typical findings include membrane blebbing, mitochondrial swelling, and dilation of the ER with detachment of ribosomes. Nuclear alterations such as pyknosis, karyorrhexis, and karyolysis are characteristic of irreversible cell injury and necrosis, not reversible injury. Therefore, nuclear alteration is the best answer. Note that the option says “constriction of ER”; classically, ER dilation is described in reversible injury.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Reversible injury → Cell swelling

  • Plasma membrane → Blebbing

  • Mitochondria → Swelling

  • ER → Dilation + ribosomal detachment

  • Nuclear changes → Irreversible injury/necrosis

Exam Pearl: Nuclear changes (pyknosis, karyorrhexis, karyolysis) indicate irreversible cell injury.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩) Which is example of caseous necrosis?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Caseous necrosis is classically associated with tuberculosis, where the necrotic tissue has a soft, cheese-like appearance. However, cat-scratch disease caused by Bartonella henselae produces necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis, which can show caseation-like necrosis. Therefore, among the given options, cat-scratch disease is the best answer. In contrast, an abscess typically produces liquefactive necrosis, myocardial infarction (MI) produces coagulative necrosis, and vasculitis may produce fibrinoid necrosis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Caseous necrosis → Tuberculosis

  • Cat-scratch disease → Necrotizing granulomatous lymphadenitis

  • Abscess → Liquefactive necrosis

  • MI → Coagulative necrosis

  • Vasculitis → May show fibrinoid necrosis

Exam Pearl: Caseous = “cheese-like” necrosis → think TB; cat-scratch disease can also show caseating/necrotizing granulomas.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪) Which is initiator caspases?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Initiator caspases are activated early in the apoptotic pathway and then activate executioner caspases. Caspase-9 is the major initiator caspase of the intrinsic (mitochondrial) apoptotic pathway. Cytochrome c released from mitochondria combines with Apaf-1 to form the apoptosome, which activates caspase-9. Caspase-9 then activates executioner caspases, mainly caspase-3 and caspase-7. Caspase-3 and caspase-6 are executioner caspases. Caspase-4 is associated with inflammatory/caspase pathways rather than being the classic apoptotic initiator tested here.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Initiator caspase → Caspase-8, Caspase-9

  • Intrinsic pathway → Caspase-9

  • Extrinsic pathway → Caspase-8

  • Executioner → Caspase-3, 6, 7

  • Intrinsic pathway → Mitochondria → cytochrome c → apoptosome

Exam Pearl: Caspase-9 = intrinsic apoptotic initiator; Caspase-3 = executioner.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫) Annexin V staining is commonly used to identify........?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Annexin V staining is commonly used to identify apoptotic cells, especially in the early stages of apoptosis. During apoptosis, phosphatidylserine (PS) normally located on the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane becomes exposed on the outer surface. Annexin V binds specifically to exposed phosphatidylserine in the presence of calcium, allowing apoptotic cells to be detected. It is commonly combined with propidium iodide (PI) to distinguish early apoptosis from late apoptosis/necrosis. Early apoptotic cells are typically Annexin V positive and PI negative.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Annexin V → Apoptosis

  • Target → Phosphatidylserine

  • PS exposure → Outer plasma membrane

  • Early apoptosis → Annexin V⁺ / PI⁻

  • Late apoptosis/necrosis → Annexin V⁺ / PI⁺

Exam Pearl: Annexin V binds exposed phosphatidylserine → marker of apoptosis.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬) What is the average amount of water loss in an adult patient of DKA with moderate severity?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In an adult patient with moderate diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), the average water deficit is approximately 5 liters. DKA causes significant fluid loss because hyperglycemia produces osmotic diuresis, leading to loss of water along with sodium, potassium, and other electrolytes. The degree of dehydration varies with the severity and duration of DKA. A commonly used exam figure is approximately 5–7 L of fluid deficit in moderate DKA, making 5 L the best answer among the options.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Moderate DKA → water deficit ≈ 5 L

  • Main cause → Osmotic diuresis

  • Losses → Water + Na⁺ + K⁺

  • Severe DKA → Greater fluid deficit

  • Treatment → IV fluid replacement + insulin + electrolyte monitoring

Exam Pearl: Moderate DKA → approximately 5 L water deficit.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭) Which is the ECG finding of hypothyroidism?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hypothyroidism commonly produces low-voltage ECG complexes, mainly due to reduced cardiac activity and, in some patients, pericardial effusion. Other ECG findings can include sinus bradycardia, prolonged PR interval, and nonspecific ST-T changes. In contrast, sinus tachycardia is more typical of hyperthyroidism. ST elevation and tall T waves are not characteristic findings of hypothyroidism.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypothyroidism → Low-voltage ECG

  • Common rhythm → Sinus bradycardia

  • May have → Pericardial effusion

  • Hyperthyroidism → Sinus tachycardia + increased cardiac activity

Exam Pearl: Low-voltage ECG + bradycardia → think hypothyroidism.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮) What is the nature of fever in pyogenic liver abscess?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Fever in a pyogenic liver abscess is classically remittent, often accompanied by high fever, chills, and rigors. The temperature fluctuates during the day but does not return to normal. This reflects the ongoing bacterial infection and inflammatory response. Pyogenic liver abscess commonly presents with fever, right upper quadrant pain, and tender hepatomegaly. Intermittent fever, by contrast, returns to normal between febrile episodes and is classically associated with conditions such as malaria.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pyogenic liver abscess → Remittent fever

  • Common symptoms → Fever + RUQ pain + tender hepatomegaly

  • Often associated with → Chills and rigors

  • Intermittent fever → Temperature returns to normal between episodes

Exam Pearl: Pyogenic liver abscess → high-grade remittent fever with chills and rigors.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯) In which of the following condition the ascitic fluid becomes serious?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In cirrhosis of the liver, ascitic fluid is typically clear, pale yellow (straw-colored), and serous. It is usually a transudative-type fluid, resulting mainly from portal hypertension and hypoalbuminemia. In contrast, ascites due to tuberculosis, malignancy, or infection is generally exudative, with higher protein content and often a higher cell count. Therefore, among the given options, cirrhosis of the liver is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Cirrhosis → clear, straw-colored serous ascites

  • TB → Usually exudative, lymphocyte-rich

  • Malignancy → Exudative, may be hemorrhagic

  • Infection → May be turbid/purulent

Exam Pearl: Serous/straw-colored ascitic fluid → classically seen in cirrhosis.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১০) Hepatitis E can produce.....?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hepatitis E virus (HEV) usually causes an acute, self-limiting hepatitis and does not typically cause chronic hepatitis or a carrier state in immunocompetent individuals. However, HEV can cause acute fulminant hepatitis (acute liver failure), particularly in pregnant women, especially during the third trimester. The mortality risk is significantly increased in this group. Chronic HEV infection can rarely occur in immunosuppressed patients, but for standard exam questions, the classic answer is acute fulminant hepatitis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • HEV → Acute hepatitis

  • Important complication → Fulminant hepatitis

  • Highest risk → Pregnancy, especially 3rd trimester

  • Chronic infection → Rare, mainly immunosuppressed

  • HCC/carrier state → Not classically associated

Exam Pearl: HEV + pregnancy → think fulminant hepatic failure.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১১) In which condition skin rash appears at 6th day of fever?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In enteric (typhoid) fever, the characteristic skin rash is rose spots, which typically appear around the 7th–10th day of illness, although they may appear around the 6th day in some exam references. They are small, faint, salmon-colored macules found mainly on the trunk and usually disappear within a few days. Dengue may cause a maculopapular rash around the time of defervescence, while measles and chickenpox have different characteristic rash patterns and timelines.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Enteric fever → Rose spots

  • Typical timing → Around 6th–10th day

  • Location → Mainly trunk

  • Rose spots → Salmon-colored, blanching macules

  • Cause → Salmonella Typhi/Paratyphi

Exam Pearl: Rose spots appearing around day 6–10 → think enteric (typhoid) fever.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১২) Persistent mild jaundice indicates.....?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Gilbert’s syndrome causes persistent or recurrent mild jaundice, usually due to an inherited reduction in UGT1A1 (UDP-glucuronosyltransferase) activity, resulting in mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Jaundice is often triggered by fasting, stress, illness, or dehydration, while liver function is otherwise normal. Acute viral hepatitis and drug-induced hepatitis generally produce more significant jaundice with elevated liver enzymes. Leptospirosis can cause marked jaundice, often with systemic illness and renal involvement.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Mild persistent/recurrent jaundice → Gilbert syndrome

  • Bilirubin → Unconjugated

  • Cause → ↓ UGT1A1 activity

  • Triggered by → Fasting, stress, illness

  • LFTs → Usually normal

Exam Pearl: Young patient + mild unconjugated jaundice + normal LFTs = Gilbert syndrome.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৩) What is not extra-abdominal cause of abdominal pain?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Several extra-abdominal conditions can present with abdominal pain. Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) commonly causes abdominal pain due to metabolic disturbances. Henoch-Schönlein purpura (IgA vasculitis) can cause significant abdominal pain from intestinal vasculitis and edema. Polyarteritis nodosa can also cause abdominal pain due to mesenteric vascular involvement and ischemia. Cushing's syndrome, however, is not a typical extra-abdominal cause of acute abdominal pain.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • DKA → Abdominal pain

  • HSP/IgA vasculitis → Abdominal pain

  • Polyarteritis nodosa → Abdominal pain

  • Cushing syndrome → Not a typical cause

Exam Pearl: DKA + HSP + PAN can mimic acute abdomen; Cushing syndrome does not.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৪) Which is not one of the characteristic triad of Zollinger–Ellison syndrome?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The classic features of Zollinger–Ellison syndrome (ZES) are gastrinoma, marked gastric acid hypersecretion, and severe/recurrent peptic ulcer disease. The ulcers may be multiple, recurrent, or occur in unusual locations such as the distal duodenum or jejunum. Although proton-pump inhibitors (PPIs) are highly effective in controlling acid secretion and symptoms, “heals with PPI” is not one of the characteristic triad. Therefore, B is the correct answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ZES triad → Gastrinoma + gastric acid hypersecretion + severe peptic ulceration

  • Gastrinoma → Usually arises in the pancreas/duodenal region

  • Hormone secreted → Gastrin

  • Treatment → High-dose PPI

  • Associated syndrome → MEN 1

Exam Pearl: Zollinger–Ellison = Gastrinoma → ↑ gastrin → ↑ acid → severe/recurrent ulcers.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৫) Which is oncogenic?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Schistosoma haematobium is considered oncogenic because chronic infection is strongly associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder. Repeated deposition of parasite eggs in the bladder wall causes chronic inflammation, granuloma formation, fibrosis, and epithelial changes that increase cancer risk.

The other options are not classically associated with malignancy:

  • Ascaris lumbricoides → intestinal helminth infection

  • Entamoeba histolytica → amoebic dysentery/liver abscess

  • Fasciola hepatica → hepatic/biliary disease

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • S. haematobium → Bladder squamous cell carcinoma

  • S. japonicum → Associated with colorectal/hepatobiliary malignancy risk

  • Chronic schistosomiasis → Egg-induced granulomatous inflammation

Exam Pearl: Schistosoma haematobium = bladder cancer.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৬) Which is not true about viral pneumonia?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Viral pneumonia typically has a more gradual onset, often preceded by upper respiratory tract symptoms such as fever, malaise, headache, and myalgia. A dry cough is common, and leukopenia may occur, particularly with some viral infections. Chest X-ray may initially be normal in mild or early disease, although bilateral/interstitial infiltrates can develop. Abrupt onset is more characteristic of bacterial pneumonia, particularly pneumococcal pneumonia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Viral pneumonia → Gradual onset

  • Cough → Usually dry

  • WBC → May show leukopenia

  • CXR → May be normal early, or show interstitial/bilateral infiltrates

  • Bacterial pneumonia → More commonly abrupt onset

Exam Pearl: Abrupt onset + productive cough + lobar consolidation → think bacterial pneumonia.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৭) All of the followings are cause of unilateral pleural effusion except?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Congestive cardiac failure (CCF) classically causes bilateral pleural effusion due to increased hydrostatic pressure in the pulmonary circulation. Although CCF can occasionally produce an asymmetric or even unilateral effusion, it is not the typical cause of unilateral pleural effusion. In contrast, pneumonia, tuberculosis, and bronchial carcinoma commonly produce unilateral pleural effusions.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Unilateral pleural effusion → Pneumonia, TB, malignancy

  • CCF → Usually bilateral

  • CCF effusion → Typically transudative

  • Malignancy/TB → Usually exudative

Exam Pearl: Unilateral pleural effusion → think infection or malignancy; CCF classically causes bilateral effusion.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৮) The drug Orlistat is used in.....?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Orlistat is a medication used in the treatment of obesity. It works by inhibiting gastric and pancreatic lipases, reducing the digestion and absorption of dietary fat by approximately 30%. The undigested fat is then excreted in the feces. Common adverse effects include oily stools, fecal urgency, and flatulence. Because it reduces fat absorption, long-term use can also reduce absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Orlistat → Obesity

  • Mechanism → Gastric + pancreatic lipase inhibitor

  • Effect → ↓ Dietary fat absorption

  • Adverse effects → Steatorrhea, oily stool, fecal urgency

  • May reduce absorption of → Vitamins A, D, E, K

Exam Pearl: Orlistat = lipase inhibitor → ↓ fat absorption → weight loss.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৯) Wilson’s disease occurs due to abnormal metabolism of which particle?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Wilson’s disease is an inherited disorder of copper metabolism caused by mutations in the ATP7B gene. This leads to impaired incorporation of copper into ceruloplasmin and reduced biliary excretion of copper, resulting in copper accumulation, particularly in the liver, brain, and cornea. Typical findings include hepatic disease, neurological/psychiatric manifestations, and Kayser–Fleischer rings.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Wilson’s disease → Copper (Cu)

  • Gene → ATP7B

  • ↓ biliary copper excretion → Copper accumulation

  • ↓ ceruloplasmin

  • Kayser–Fleischer ring → Cornea

Exam Pearl: Wilson = Copper accumulation due to ATP7B defect.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২০) Thick & thin film are used for diagnosis of.....?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Thick and thin blood films are classically used for the diagnosis of malaria caused by Plasmodium species.

  • Thick film → More sensitive for detecting malaria parasites because a larger volume of blood is concentrated in a smaller area.

  • Thin film → Better for species identification and assessing parasite morphology and parasitemia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Thick film → Detection

  • Thin film → Species identification

  • Malaria parasite → Plasmodium

  • Common species → P. falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, P. ovale

Exam Pearl: Thick = find the parasite; thin = identify the species.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২১) Minor criteria for diagnosis of rheumatic fever excludes.......?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
According to the Jones criteria, polyarthritis is a major criterion, not a minor criterion, for the diagnosis of acute rheumatic fever. The minor criteria include fever, elevated ESR/CRP, prolonged PR interval, and arthralgia (depending on the applicable Jones criteria version). Leukocytosis may occur in acute rheumatic fever but is not a formal Jones minor criterion. However, among the given options, polyarthritis is clearly the intended answer because it is a major criterion.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Major criteria: Carditis, arthritis, chorea, erythema marginatum, subcutaneous nodules

  • Minor criteria: Fever, arthralgia, ↑ ESR/CRP, prolonged PR interval

  • Polyarthritis → Major criterion

  • High ESR → Minor criterion

Exam Pearl: Polyarthritis = Major; fever + ↑ ESR/CRP = Minor.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২২) Which somatoform disorder is also known as health anxiety?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hypochondriacal disorder, now broadly termed illness anxiety disorder, is characterized by excessive preoccupation with having or developing a serious illness, despite little or no objective evidence of disease. It is therefore commonly referred to as health anxiety. Patients may frequently seek medical reassurance or repeatedly check their body for symptoms.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Health anxiety → Hypochondriacal disorder

  • Modern term → Illness anxiety disorder

  • Main feature → Fear/preoccupation with serious illness

  • Somatization disorder → Multiple physical symptoms

    • Conversion disorder → Neurological symptoms without adequate organic explanation

    Exam Pearl: Hypochondriasis = excessive fear of illness = health anxiety.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৩) Calcipotriol is a mainstay of primary care management of which disease?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Calcipotriol is a synthetic vitamin D₃ analogue and an important topical treatment for psoriasis. It works by regulating keratinocyte proliferation and differentiation, thereby reducing the excessive epidermal growth characteristic of psoriasis. It is commonly used for mild-to-moderate plaque psoriasis, either alone or in combination with a topical corticosteroid.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Calcipotriol → Psoriasis

  • Class → Vitamin D₃ analogue

  • Action → ↓ keratinocyte proliferation + promotes differentiation

  • Common use → Plaque psoriasis

  • Often combined with → Topical corticosteroid

Exam Pearl: Calcipotriol = topical vitamin D analogue → psoriasis.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৪) Which one isn't an extra pulmonary effects of COPD?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
COPD has several systemic/extra-pulmonary effects due to chronic inflammation and its associated metabolic consequences. These include altered fat metabolism, skeletal muscle weakness, and impaired renal salt and water handling, particularly in advanced disease. COPD is associated with increased, not decreased, systemic inflammatory activity and circulating inflammatory markers such as CRP and certain cytokines. Therefore, decrease circulating inflammatory markers is not an extra-pulmonary effect of COPD.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • COPD → Systemic inflammation ↑

  • Fat metabolism → Altered

  • Skeletal muscle → Weakness/wasting

  • Renal function → Impaired salt & water excretion

  • Inflammatory markers → Generally increased

Exam Pearl: COPD is a systemic inflammatory disease—not just a lung disease.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৫) Which is sterilization method for endoscope?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Endoscopes are heat-sensitive medical instruments, so methods such as dry heat, boiling, or standard steam sterilization can damage them. Ethylene oxide (EtO) gas is a low-temperature sterilization method suitable for heat- and moisture-sensitive equipment. It penetrates complex instrument surfaces and can achieve sterilization without exposing the endoscope to high temperatures.

Note: In modern practice, flexible endoscopes are often processed with high-level disinfection or low-temperature sterilization systems depending on the device and local guidelines. But for this MCQ, ethylene oxide is the intended answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Endoscope → Ethylene oxide (EtO)

  • EtO → Low-temperature sterilization

  • Heat-sensitive equipment → EtO

  • Dry heat → High temperature

  • Boiling → Disinfection, not reliable sterilization

Exam Pearl: Heat-sensitive endoscope → think low-temperature EtO sterilization.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৬) Which is a hallmark of Ankylosing spondylitis?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Syndesmophyte formation is a hallmark radiological feature of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). Syndesmophytes are thin, vertically oriented bony bridges that form along the outer fibers of the annulus fibrosus, eventually bridging adjacent vertebral bodies and producing the classic “bamboo spine” appearance. Ankylosing spondylitis is a seronegative spondyloarthropathy strongly associated with HLA-B27. Restriction of spinal movement can occur, but it is a clinical consequence rather than the characteristic radiological hallmark.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ankylosing spondylitis → Syndesmophytes

  • X-ray → Bamboo spine

  • Association → HLA-B27

  • Typical pain → Inflammatory back pain

  • Osteophytes → More typical of osteoarthritis

Exam Pearl: AS = marginal syndesmophytes → bamboo spine.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৭) A 70 years male presented with anemia, infection, painless lymphadenopathy with systemic symptoms. What is most likely diagnosis?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A 70-year-old man with anemia, recurrent infections, painless lymphadenopathy, and systemic symptoms strongly suggests Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL). CLL is the most common leukemia in older adults and is characterized by accumulation of mature but functionally abnormal B lymphocytes. Anemia may develop due to bone marrow infiltration or autoimmune hemolysis, while recurrent infections occur because of hypogammaglobulinemia and impaired immune function. Painless generalized lymphadenopathy is also a common clinical feature.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Elderly + painless lymphadenopathy + recurrent infection → CLL

  • CLL cell → Mature B lymphocyte

  • Common complication → Hypogammaglobulinemia → recurrent infections

  • Peripheral smear → Smudge cells

  • CLL is the adult counterpart of SLL

Exam Pearl: Old patient + lymphocytosis + painless lymphadenopathy + recurrent infections = CLL.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৮) Ophthalmia neonatorum is caused by....?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Ophthalmia neonatorum is neonatal conjunctivitis occurring within the first 28 days of life. Among the given options, Neisseria gonorrhoeae is the classic causative organism and can cause severe, rapidly progressive conjunctivitis with profuse purulent discharge and corneal ulceration/perforation. It is acquired during passage through an infected birth canal. Chlamydia trachomatis is another important cause of neonatal conjunctivitis, but it is not listed here.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ophthalmia neonatorum → N. gonorrhoeae

  • Severe purulent conjunctivitis → Gonococcus

  • Major complication → Corneal ulcer/perforation

  • Another important cause → C. trachomatis

  • Prevention → Neonatal ocular prophylaxis according to local guidelines

Exam Pearl: Profuse purulent neonatal conjunctivitis → think N. gonorrhoeae.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৯) Which is X-linked dominant diseases?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Vitamin-D resistant rickets (hypophosphatemic rickets) is classically an X-linked dominant disorder, caused most commonly by mutations in the PHEX gene. It causes renal phosphate wasting, resulting in defective bone mineralization and rickets that does not respond adequately to ordinary doses of vitamin D.

The other options are also genetic disorders but have different inheritance patterns: Huntington disease, neurofibromatosis type 1, and Marfan syndrome are autosomal dominant.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • X-linked dominant → Vitamin-D resistant (hypophosphatemic) rickets

  • Huntington disease → Autosomal dominant

  • Neurofibromatosis type 1 → Autosomal dominant

  • Marfan syndrome → Autosomal dominant

  • X-linked dominant → Both sexes affected; no father-to-son transmission

Exam Pearl: Vitamin-D resistant rickets = classic X-linked dominant disorder.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩০) Which is coagulase positive?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Staphylococcus aureus is coagulase-positive, which is an important laboratory feature used to distinguish it from most other clinically important staphylococci. Coagulase converts fibrinogen to fibrin, causing plasma to clot. S. epidermidis and S. saprophyticus are coagulase-negative staphylococci. Streptococcus pyogenes is a streptococcus and is not classified by the coagulase test.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Coagulase positive → S. aureus

  • Coagulase negative → S. epidermidis, S. saprophyticus

  • S. aureus → Gram-positive cocci in clusters

  • S. aureus → Catalase positive + coagulase positive

Exam Pearl: Coagulase-positive staphylococcus = S. aureus.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩১) Which one is 1st line drug for focal seizure?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
For focal (partial-onset) seizures, levetiracetam is a commonly recommended first-line antiseizure medication, along with options such as lamotrigine depending on the guideline and patient factors. Levetiracetam is widely used because it has few drug interactions, is generally well tolerated, and can be used in both focal and generalized seizure types. Ethosuximide is specifically used for absence seizures, while sodium valproate is particularly useful for generalized epilepsies.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Focal seizure → Levetiracetam / Lamotrigine

  • Absence seizure → Ethosuximide

  • Generalized tonic-clonic → Valproate (with important reproductive considerations)

  • Levetiracetam → Few drug interactions

Exam Pearl: Focal seizure → think levetiracetam or lamotrigine.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩২) Sudden neurological dysfunction due to cerebral ischemia lasting less than 24 hours and the patient recovers completely within 24 hours is termed as.......?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA) is a transient episode of neurological dysfunction caused by focal brain, spinal cord, or retinal ischemia without acute infarction. Historically, TIA was defined as neurological symptoms lasting less than 24 hours with complete recovery. Modern definitions emphasize absence of tissue infarction, rather than simply the duration of symptoms. RIND (Reversible Ischemic Neurological Deficit) is an older term for deficits lasting more than 24 hours but resolving within days, and is no longer commonly used.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • TIA → transient focal neurological dysfunction due to ischemia

  • Traditional definition → <24 hours

  • Modern definition → No acute infarction

  • RIND → Older term, symptoms >24 hours but reversible

  • Complete stroke → Persistent neurological deficit

Exam Pearl: Transient neurological deficit + complete recovery within 24 h = TIA (traditional definition).

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৩) Which is antidote for opioids poisoning?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Naloxone is the specific opioid antagonist used to reverse opioid poisoning, particularly life-threatening respiratory depression. It rapidly displaces opioids from μ-opioid receptors, restoring respiratory drive. Because naloxone has a relatively short duration of action compared with some opioids, repeated doses or continuous infusion may be required in severe poisoning.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Opioid poisoning → Naloxone

  • Mechanism → μ-opioid receptor antagonist

  • Main life-threatening feature → Respiratory depression

  • Pralidoxime → Organophosphate poisoning

  • Flumazenil → Benzodiazepine toxicity

  • Dimercaprol → Heavy-metal poisoning

Exam Pearl: Opioid overdose + respiratory depression → Naloxone.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৪) Coated tongue is significant in......?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A coated tongue is a classic clinical finding in enteric (typhoid) fever. The tongue may have a thick white coating centrally, with a relatively red, clean tip and margins, sometimes described as a “typhoid tongue.” It occurs along with systemic features such as prolonged fever, malaise, abdominal symptoms, and relative bradycardia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Coated tongue → Enteric fever

  • Typhoid tongue → White-coated center + red tip/margins

  • Syphilis → Oral mucous patches may occur

  • Parkinsonism → Bradykinesia, rigidity, resting tremor

  • Acromegaly → Enlarged tongue (macroglossia)

Exam Pearl: White-coated tongue with red tip and margins → think enteric (typhoid) fever.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৫) Which is not a feature of tetanus?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Tetanus is caused by Clostridium tetani toxin (tetanospasmin), which blocks inhibitory neurotransmission by inhibiting GABA and glycine release. This produces muscle rigidity and painful spasms, not flaccid paralysis. Classic features include lockjaw (trismus), dysphagia, and opisthotonus (marked backward arching of the body).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Tetanus → Spastic/rigid paralysis

  • Lockjaw (trismus)

  • Dysphagia

  • Opisthotonus

  • Toxin → Blocks GABA + glycine

Exam Pearl: Tetanus = rigidity and spasms, not flaccidity.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৬) What is the reason behind Apraxic gait in old people?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Apraxic gait (gait apraxia) in elderly people is classically associated with bilateral cerebral hemisphere dysfunction, particularly involving the frontal lobes and their subcortical connections. Patients have difficulty initiating and coordinating walking despite having adequate muscle strength and intact basic motor and sensory function. It is commonly seen in normal-pressure hydrocephalus and some forms of vascular dementia. The gait is often described as “magnetic” or “stuck to the floor.”

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Apraxic gait → Bilateral frontal/cerebral hemisphere dysfunction

  • Common association → Normal-pressure hydrocephalus

  • Gait → Magnetic/shuffling

  • Proximal myopathy → Waddling gait

  • Sensory neuropathy → Sensory ataxic gait

Exam Pearl: Elderly patient + magnetic/apraxic gait → think frontal lobe dysfunction or NPH.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৭) Where does detoxification of drugs occur?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Drug detoxification occurs mainly in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) of hepatocytes. The SER contains the microsomal cytochrome P450 enzyme system, which performs many Phase I reactions such as oxidation, reduction, and hydroxylation of drugs. These reactions often make drugs more water-soluble and prepare them for subsequent Phase II conjugation and excretion.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Drug detoxification → Smooth ER

  • Main organ → Liver

  • Key enzyme system → Cytochrome P450

  • Phase I → Oxidation, reduction, hydroxylation

  • Rough ER → Mainly protein synthesis

Exam Pearl: Smooth ER + cytochrome P450 = drug detoxification.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৮) What is the lifespan of average erythrocyte in newborn?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The average lifespan of an erythrocyte in a newborn is shorter than in an adult. In newborns, RBC lifespan is approximately 60–90 days, with 80 days being the commonly accepted exam value. In adults, the normal erythrocyte lifespan is approximately 120 days. The shorter neonatal RBC lifespan contributes to the increased bilirubin production seen after birth and is one factor in physiological neonatal jaundice.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Newborn RBC lifespan → ~80 days

  • Adult RBC lifespan → ~120 days

  • Shorter neonatal lifespan → ↑ bilirubin production

  • Physiological neonatal jaundice → partly due to increased RBC turnover

Exam Pearl: RBC lifespan: newborn ≈ 80 days; adult ≈ 120 days.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৯) Which one is not included in hazards of massive blood transfusion?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Thrombophlebitis is not a typical complication of massive blood transfusion. Massive transfusion can cause several metabolic and hematological complications, including hyperkalemia from potassium released by stored RBCs, citrate toxicity causing hypocalcemia, and acid–base disturbances. Hypothermia, dilutional coagulopathy, and transfusion reactions are also important complications.

Metabolic acidosis can occur during massive transfusion, particularly early in the process, although stored blood undergoes changes that can produce complex acid–base effects.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Massive transfusion → Hyperkalemia

  • Citrate toxicity → Hypocalcemia

  • → Hypothermia

  • → Dilutional coagulopathy

  • Thrombophlebitis → Not a typical hazard

Exam Pearl: Massive transfusion hazards = hypothermia + hypocalcemia + hyperkalemia + coagulopathy.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪০) Shooting star appearance on dark ground illumination for which organism?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Vibrio cholerae shows characteristic rapid, darting (“shooting star”) motility on dark-field/dark-ground illumination. This is due to its single polar flagellum, which allows rapid movement. The organism is a curved, comma-shaped, Gram-negative bacillus.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Shooting star/darting motility → V. cholerae

  • Motility → Rapid, darting

  • Flagella → Single polar flagellum

  • Shape → Comma-shaped

  • Gram stain → Gram-negative curved bacillus

Exam Pearl: Dark-field + shooting-star motility = Vibrio cholerae.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪১) What is the speed of conduction (m/s) for Bundle of His?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The Bundle of His conducts electrical impulses rapidly from the AV node toward the ventricles. Its conduction velocity is approximately 0.5 m/s. This rapid conduction is essential for transmitting the impulse efficiently through the bundle branches and Purkinje system, producing coordinated ventricular contraction.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • AV node → Slowest conduction (~0.05 m/s)

  • Bundle of His → ~0.5 m/s

  • Purkinje fibers → Fastest (~4 m/s)

  • Atrial/ventricular muscle → ~0.3–0.5 m/s

Exam Pearl: Bundle of His = 0.5 m/s; Purkinje fibers = ~4 m/s.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪২) What doesn’t increases Heart Rate?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Raised intracranial pressure (ICP) does not directly increase heart rate. In fact, significant elevation of ICP can produce the Cushing reflex, characterized by hypertension, bradycardia, and irregular respiration. The bradycardia occurs due to increased vagal activity in response to the elevated arterial pressure.

The other options generally increase heart rate:

  • Temperature ↑ → HR ↑

  • Adrenaline → β₁ stimulation → HR ↑

  • Muscular exercise → sympathetic activation → HR ↑

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Raised ICP → Cushing triad

    • Hypertension

    • Bradycardia

    • Irregular respiration

  • Adrenaline → Tachycardia

  • Exercise → Tachycardia

  • Fever → Tachycardia

Exam Pearl: Raised ICP → bradycardia, not tachycardia.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৩) What is the percentage of total blood within veins??
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Veins are the major capacitance (blood reservoir) vessels of the circulation. Approximately 64% of the total blood volume is present in the systemic veins and venules at rest. This large volume can be mobilized by sympathetic venoconstriction when necessary, helping maintain venous return and cardiac output.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Veins & venules → ~64% of total blood volume

  • Arteries → ~13%

  • Capillaries → ~7%

  • Heart → ~7%

  • Veins = capacitance vessels / blood reservoir

Exam Pearl: ~64% of blood is stored in the veins.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৪) How physiological dead space is measured?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Physiological dead space is measured using the Bohr equation, which relates the partial pressure of CO₂ in expired air to arterial CO₂:

VD/VT=PaCO2−PEˉCO2PaCO2VD​/VT​=PaCO2​​PaCO2​​−PEˉCO2​​​

It estimates the proportion of each tidal breath that does not participate effectively in gas exchange.

Fowler’s method is mainly used to measure anatomical dead space, using the single-breath nitrogen washout technique.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Physiological dead space → Bohr equation

  • Anatomical dead space → Fowler method

  • Helium dilution → FRC measurement

  • Nitrogen washout → FRC/anatomical dead-space assessment

Exam Pearl: Bohr = physiological dead space; Fowler = anatomical dead space.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৫) Which is the smallest bacteria?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Mycoplasma is the smallest free-living bacterium and is notable for lacking a cell wall. Its small size allows it to pass through filters that normally retain larger bacteria. Because it lacks peptidoglycan, β-lactam antibiotics such as penicillins and cephalosporins are ineffective against it.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Smallest free-living bacterium → Mycoplasma

  • Cell wall → Absent

  • Shape → Pleomorphic

  • β-lactams → Ineffective

  • Common species → Mycoplasma pneumoniae

Exam Pearl: Smallest bacterium + no cell wall = Mycoplasma.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৬) Specific gravity of gall bladder bile is…?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The specific gravity of gallbladder bile is approximately 1.030. Bile stored in the gallbladder becomes concentrated because water and electrolytes are absorbed through the gallbladder wall. Therefore, gallbladder bile has a higher specific gravity than hepatic bile.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Gallbladder bile → Specific gravity ≈ 1.030

  • Hepatic bile → More dilute

  • Gallbladder → Concentrates bile

  • Main function → Storage and concentration of bile

Exam Pearl: Gallbladder bile SG ≈ 1.03.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৭) Evans blue dye indicator is used for the measurement of......?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Evans blue dye is used to measure plasma volume because it binds strongly to plasma albumin and therefore remains largely within the intravascular compartment.

The dye is injected intravenously, and its concentration after equilibration is used to calculate plasma volume.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Evans blue → Plasma volume

  • D₂O / tritiated water → Total body water

  • Inulin → ECF volume

  • Radioactive potassium → ICF volume

  • Plasma volume + RBC volume → Total blood volume

Exam Pearl: Evans blue = albumin-bound dye = plasma volume.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৮) Segmentation contraction is the movement of the......?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Segmentation contractions are characteristic movements of the small intestine. They are mainly mixing contractions that divide intestinal contents into segments and repeatedly mix them with digestive juices, bringing nutrients into contact with the intestinal mucosa. They are not primarily responsible for forward propulsion.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Segmentation → Small intestine

  • Main function → Mixing + digestion + absorption

  • Peristalsis → Propulsion

  • Migrating motor complex → Fasting intestinal motility

  • Large intestine → Haustral contractions/mass movements

Exam Pearl: Segmentation = mixing movement of the small intestine.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৯) What is the percentage of sperm in semen?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Spermatozoa constitute approximately 20% of the volume of semen. The majority of semen volume comes from the secretions of the seminal vesicles, prostate, and bulbourethral glands. Seminal vesicle fluid contributes the largest portion.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Sperm → ~20% of semen

  • Seminal vesicles → ~60–70%

  • Prostate → ~25–30%

  • Bulbourethral glands → small amount

  • Sperm are produced in the seminiferous tubules

Exam Pearl: Sperm = approximately 20% of semen volume.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫০) Which is non specific test for treponema?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
VDRL (Venereal Disease Research Laboratory) test is a non-specific (non-treponemal) test for syphilis. It detects reagin antibodies directed against cardiolipin-lecithin-cholesterol antigens rather than antibodies specifically directed against Treponema pallidum.

The other options are treponemal-specific tests:

  • TPHA → Treponemal-specific

  • TPI (Treponema pallidum immobilization) → Treponemal-specific

  • FTA-ABS → Treponemal-specific

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Non-treponemal → VDRL, RPR

  • Treponemal-specific → TPHA, FTA-ABS, TPI

  • VDRL/RPR → useful for screening and monitoring treatment

  • Treponemal tests → usually remain positive for a long time

Exam Pearl: VDRL = non-treponemal test; TPHA/FTA = treponemal tests.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫১) Inability to perform sexual intercourse is called.....?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Impotency (more appropriately termed erectile dysfunction in modern terminology) refers to the inability to achieve or maintain an erection sufficient for sexual intercourse. It is different from infertility, which refers to the inability to achieve pregnancy despite regular unprotected intercourse.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Impotency → inability to perform sexual intercourse due to erectile/sexual dysfunction

  • Sterility → inability to produce viable sperm/ova

  • Infertility → inability to achieve pregnancy

  • Castration → removal or loss of gonadal function

Exam Pearl: Inability to perform sexual intercourse → Impotency (erectile dysfunction).

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫২) Which one is not a feature of hyperthyroidism?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Weight gain is not a typical feature of hyperthyroidism. Increased thyroid hormone levels raise the basal metabolic rate, causing increased calorie expenditure and usually weight loss despite increased appetite.

Typical features include excitability/nervousness, muscle weakness, heat intolerance, sweating, tremor, palpitations, and weight loss.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hyperthyroidism → Weight loss

  • → Heat intolerance

  • → Increased excitability

  • → Muscle weakness

  • → Tachycardia/palpitations

  • Hypothyroidism → Weight gain + cold intolerance

Exam Pearl: Hyperthyroidism burns energy → weight loss, not weight gain.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৩) Which hormone has receptor in nucleus?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Steroid hormones have intracellular receptors, mainly located in the cytoplasm or nucleus. The hormone–receptor complex enters or acts within the nucleus and binds to DNA, regulating gene transcription.

Thyroid hormones are the important exception among the listed non-steroid hormones: their receptor is also located in the nucleus. Therefore, if the question asks “Which hormone has a receptor in the nucleus?”, both thyroxine (T3/T4) and steroid hormones can have nuclear receptors.

However, in a single-best-answer MCQ, if the intended classification is “hormones with intracellular/nuclear receptors,” B) Steroid is usually the expected answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Steroid hormones → intracellular/nuclear receptors

  • Thyroid hormones → nuclear receptors

  • PTH → cell-surface GPCR

  • GH → cell-surface cytokine receptor (JAK-STAT)

Exam Pearl: Steroid + thyroid hormones → intracellular/nuclear receptors.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৪) Which is the commonest cell group in anterior pituitary?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Somatotrophs are the most abundant cell type in the anterior pituitary (adenohypophysis), comprising roughly 40–50% of anterior pituitary cells. They secrete growth hormone (GH), which promotes body growth partly through stimulation of IGF-1 (somatomedin C) production.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common anterior pituitary cell → Somatotroph

  • Somatotroph → GH

  • Mammotroph/Lactotroph → Prolactin

  • Corticotroph → ACTH

  • Thyrotroph → TSH

Exam Pearl: Anterior pituitary's most abundant cell = somatotroph → GH.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৫) Which fungus is capsulated?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Cryptococcus neoformans is a capsulated yeast with a prominent polysaccharide capsule, which is an important virulence factor. The capsule can be demonstrated by India ink staining and detected using cryptococcal antigen testing. It commonly causes meningitis, especially in immunocompromised patients.

  • Histoplasma capsulatum → despite its name, does not have a true capsule.

  • Candida albicans → yeast with pseudohyphae, not a prominent capsule.

  • Aspergillus → septate, acute-angle branching hyphae, not capsulated.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Capsulated fungus → Cryptococcus neoformans

  • Capsule → Polysaccharide

  • Demonstration → India ink

  • Major disease → Cryptococcal meningitis

Exam Pearl: “Capsule” in fungi → Cryptococcus neoformans.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৬) Which is a class-1 neurotransmitter?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In the classical classification of neurotransmitters, Class I neurotransmitters are the small-molecule acetylcholine and amino-acid neurotransmitters. However, depending on the textbook/classification system, the term “Class I” may be used differently.

For the common MBBS physiology classification:

  • Class I → Acetylcholine

  • Class II → Amino acids (GABA, glutamate, glycine)

  • Class III → Monoamines (dopamine, noradrenaline, serotonin)

  • Class IV → Neuropeptides

Therefore, among the given options, acetylcholine is the expected answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Class I → Acetylcholine

  • GABA → Amino-acid neurotransmitter

  • Dopamine → Monoamine

  • Nitric oxide → Gaseous/non-classical neurotransmitter

Exam Pearl: Class I neurotransmitter = Acetylcholine (ACh).

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৭) Which one is a superficial reflex?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The cremasteric reflex is a superficial (cutaneous) reflex. Stroking the medial aspect of the upper thigh causes contraction of the cremaster muscle and elevation of the ipsilateral testis. The afferent limb mainly travels via the ilioinguinal nerve (L1), while the efferent limb is via the genital branch of the genitofemoral nerve (L1–L2).

The other options are not superficial cutaneous reflexes:

  • Vomiting → visceral reflex

  • Light reflex → pupillary autonomic reflex

  • Jaw jerk → deep tendon reflex

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Superficial reflex → Cremasteric

  • Plantar reflex → superficial

  • Abdominal reflex → superficial

  • Jaw jerk → deep reflex

  • Knee jerk → deep tendon reflex

Exam Pearl: Cremasteric reflex = superficial reflex (L1–L2).

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৮) Inability to perform rapidly alternating movement is called...?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Dysdiadochokinesia is the inability to perform rapid, alternating movements smoothly and accurately. It is a classic sign of cerebellar dysfunction, particularly involving the cerebellar hemispheres.

Examples include difficulty rapidly alternating pronation and supination of the forearm.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Rapid alternating movement impaired → Dysdiadochokinesia

  • Past pointing → Overshooting/undershooting a target

  • Dysmetria → Inaccurate range/distance of movement

  • Dysarthria → Difficulty in articulation of speech

  • Cerebellar lesion → Ataxia + dysmetria + dysdiadochokinesia

Exam Pearl: “Rapid alternating movements” → Dysdiadochokinesia.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৯) Which receptor is concerned with pressure & vibration?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pacinian (lamellar) corpuscles are mechanoreceptors that detect deep pressure and vibration, particularly high-frequency vibration. They are rapidly adapting receptors and are found deep in the dermis, subcutaneous tissue, joints, and other deep tissues.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pressure + vibration → Pacinian corpuscles

  • Light touch → Meissner corpuscles

  • Stretch → Ruffini endings

  • Muscle length → Muscle spindle

  • Muscle tension → Golgi tendon organ

  • Pain → Free nerve endings

Exam Pearl: Pacinian corpuscle = deep pressure + vibration.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬০) Which may be called proud flesh?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
“Proud flesh” refers to exuberant granulation tissue that grows excessively above the level of a wound and interferes with epithelialization. It is commonly seen in wounds undergoing healing, particularly when granulation tissue becomes excessive.

It is not the same as a keloid or hypertrophic scar, which are excessive collagen-producing scars.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Proud flesh → Exuberant granulation tissue

  • Keloid → Scar extends beyond wound margins

  • Hypertrophic scar → Raised scar within wound margins

  • Atrophic scar → Thin/depressed scar

Exam Pearl: Proud flesh = exuberant granulation tissue.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬১) Which nerve is not related to taste sensation?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The trigeminal nerve (CN V) is not a taste nerve. It provides general somatic sensation from the oral cavity and tongue, such as touch, pain, and temperature, but it does not carry special visceral afferent taste fibers.

Taste sensation is carried by:

  • Facial nerve (CN VII) → anterior 2/3 of tongue

  • Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) → posterior 1/3

  • Vagus nerve (CN X) → epiglottis/root of tongue

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Taste anterior 2/3 → CN VII

  • Taste posterior 1/3 → CN IX

  • Taste epiglottis → CN X

  • General sensation anterior 2/3 → CN V3

  • Trigeminal → no taste

Exam Pearl: Taste = VII, IX, X; general sensation = V.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬২) Genital tubercle in females gives rise to which of the following?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The genital tubercle is an embryological structure that develops into the phallus. In females, it becomes the clitoris; in males, it develops into the glans penis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Genital tubercle → Clitoris (female) / Penis (male)

  • Urogenital folds → Labia minora (female) / Ventral penis & urethra (male)

  • Labioscrotal swellings → Labia majora (female) / Scrotum (male)

  • Vagina → Mainly from sinovaginal bulbs + Müllerian ducts

Exam Pearl: Genital tubercle → Clitoris.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৩) Meckel’s diverticulum is a developmental anomaly of which part of gut?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Meckel’s diverticulum is a congenital remnant of the vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct and arises from the ileum, making it a developmental anomaly of the small intestine. It is the most common congenital anomaly of the gastrointestinal tract.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Meckel’s diverticulum → Ileum

  • Embryological remnant → Vitelline duct

  • Usually located within ~60 cm of the ileocecal valve

  • May contain ectopic gastric or pancreatic tissue

  • Complications → Bleeding, inflammation, obstruction

Exam Pearl: Meckel’s diverticulum = vitelline duct remnant in ileum.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৪) Ligamentum teres hepatis is the remnants of ____?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Ligamentum teres hepatis (round ligament of the liver) is the fibrous remnant of the left umbilical vein after birth. During fetal life, the left umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood from the placenta toward the liver.

After birth, it obliterates and becomes the ligamentum teres, located in the free margin of the falciform ligament.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ligamentum teres → Left umbilical vein

  • Ligamentum venosum → Ductus venosus

  • Medial umbilical ligament → Umbilical artery

  • Lateral umbilical ligament → Inferior epigastric vessels

Exam Pearl: Left umbilical vein → ligamentum teres hepatis.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৫) What is the type of diabetic gangrene?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Diabetic gangrene is classically considered a form of dry gangrene, particularly when it results from peripheral arterial disease and ischemia. The affected tissue becomes dry, shriveled, black, and demarcated.

However, diabetes also predisposes to infection, so a diabetic foot can develop wet (moist) gangrene when infection and tissue necrosis are prominent.

For this MCQ, the expected answer is dry gangrene.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ischemic gangrene → Dry

  • Infected gangrene → Wet/moist

  • Diabetes → peripheral vascular disease + neuropathy + infection risk

  • Diabetic foot may therefore become wet gangrene if infected

Exam Pearl: For the classic exam association: Diabetic gangrene → dry gangrene.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৬) Diploid number of chromosome is restored by which process ?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Fertilization restores the diploid (2n) chromosome number by the fusion of two haploid gametes—sperm (n) and ovum (n)—to form a diploid zygote (2n).

Spermatogenesis and oogenesis produce haploid gametes, while ovulation releases the secondary oocyte. Implantation occurs later and does not alter chromosome number.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Gametes → haploid (n)

  • Fertilization → n + n = 2n

  • Zygote → diploid

  • Meiosis → reduces 2n → n

Exam Pearl: Diploid number is restored by fertilization.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৭) Which gland does not arise from surface ectoderm?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The adrenal cortex develops from mesoderm, specifically from coelomic epithelium of the posterior abdominal wall. Therefore, it does not arise from surface ectoderm.

The other options have surface ectodermal origins:

  • Hypophysis cerebri (anterior pituitary) → oral ectoderm (Rathke’s pouch)

  • Mammary gland → surface ectoderm

  • Lacrimal gland → surface ectoderm

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Adrenal cortex → Mesoderm

  • Adrenal medulla → Neural crest

  • Anterior pituitary → Oral ectoderm

  • Mammary gland → Surface ectoderm

  • Lacrimal gland → Surface ectoderm

Exam Pearl: Adrenal cortex is mesodermal, not ectodermal.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৮) Which one is called policeman of abdomen?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The greater omentum is known as the “policeman of the abdomen” because it can migrate toward areas of inflammation or infection and wall off localized infection, helping prevent its spread throughout the peritoneal cavity.

It contains abundant fat, blood vessels, lymphatics, and immune cells and can adhere to inflamed organs.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Policeman of abdomen → Greater omentum

  • Main role → Limits spread of infection

  • Often adheres to inflamed/perforated areas

  • Contains fat + immune cells

Exam Pearl: Greater omentum = policeman of the abdomen.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৯) Portal vein is formed at the level of which vertebra?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The portal vein is formed by the union of the superior mesenteric vein (SMV) and splenic vein, usually behind the neck of the pancreas at approximately the level of the L2 vertebra.

It then ascends toward the liver in the hepatoduodenal ligament.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Portal vein formation → L2

  • Formed by → SMV + splenic vein

  • Site → Behind neck of pancreas

  • Abdominal aorta bifurcation → L4

  • IVC formation → approximately L5

Exam Pearl: Portal vein = SMV + splenic vein → L2.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭০) Which is not a feature of raised ICP?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Tachycardia is not a typical feature of raised intracranial pressure (ICP). Increased ICP can trigger the Cushing reflex, which classically produces hypertension, bradycardia, and irregular respiration.

Common features of raised ICP include headache, vomiting, and papilloedema. Vomiting may occur due to stimulation of the vomiting center, while papilloedema results from increased intracranial pressure being transmitted along the optic nerve sheath.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Raised ICP → Headache

  • → Vomiting

  • → Papilloedema

  • Severe raised ICP → Cushing triad

    • Hypertension

    • Bradycardia

    • Irregular respiration

Exam Pearl: Raised ICP → bradycardia, not tachycardia.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭১) Male homologous of vagina is-
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The prostatic utricle is considered the male homolog of the vagina and uterus. It is a small blind-ending pouch opening into the prostatic urethra and represents a remnant of the Müllerian (paramesonephric) ducts.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Prostatic utricle → homolog of vagina/uterus

  • Müllerian duct remnants in male → Prostatic utricle + appendix testis

  • Penis → homolog of clitoris

  • Scrotum → homolog of labia majora

  • Testis → homologous to ovary

Exam Pearl: Male homolog of vagina = prostatic utricle.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭২) Which one is the ventral branch of abdominal aorta?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The coeliac trunk is an unpaired ventral (anterior) branch of the abdominal aorta. It arises just below the diaphragm at approximately the T12 vertebral level and supplies the foregut.

Its three major branches are:

  • Left gastric artery

  • Splenic artery

  • Common hepatic artery

The inferior phrenic and middle suprarenal arteries are lateral branches, while the common iliac arteries are terminal branches.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ventral unpaired branches → Coeliac trunk, SMA, IMA

  • Coeliac trunk → Foregut

  • SMA → Midgut

  • IMA → Hindgut

  • Coeliac trunk origin → T12

Exam Pearl: Ventral branch of abdominal aorta = Coeliac trunk.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৩) What is space of Disse?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The Space of Disse is the perisinusoidal space located between the sinusoidal endothelial cells and hepatocytes in the liver.

It contains hepatic stellate (Ito) cells, extracellular matrix, and tissue fluid. It is an important site for exchange of substances between the blood in hepatic sinusoids and hepatocytes.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Space of Disse → Perisinusoidal space

  • Location → Between sinusoidal endothelium & hepatocytes

  • Contains → Stellate (Ito) cells

  • Function → Exchange between blood and hepatocytes

Exam Pearl: Disse = perisinusoidal space of the liver.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৪) Which is not a salivary gland?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The three major salivary glands are:

  • Parotid

  • Submandibular

  • Sublingual

Buccal glands are minor salivary glands located in the buccal mucosa. Therefore, if the question asks for a gland that is not a major salivary gland, the answer is Buccal.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Parotid → Major salivary gland

  • Submandibular → Major

  • Sublingual → Major

  • Buccal → Minor salivary gland

Exam Pearl: Major salivary glands = Parotid + Submandibular + Sublingual.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৫) Which is most common site of bone metastasis?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The spine (vertebral column) is the most common site of skeletal/bone metastasis. This is largely because of its extensive red bone marrow and rich venous network, particularly the Batson vertebral venous plexus, which provides a route for tumor cells to reach the vertebrae.

Common primary cancers that metastasize to bone include breast, prostate, lung, kidney, and thyroid cancers.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common bone metastasis → Spine

  • Other common sites → Pelvis, ribs, proximal femur

  • Vertebral spread → Batson venous plexus

  • Breast & prostate → commonly metastasize to bone

Exam Pearl: Bone metastasis → think spine first.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৬) Which is resistance vessel?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Arterioles are called the resistance vessels because they have a major role in regulating systemic vascular resistance and blood pressure. Their smooth muscle can constrict or dilate, producing large changes in resistance and controlling blood flow into capillary beds.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Arterioles → Resistance vessels

  • Veins → Capacitance vessels / blood reservoir

  • Arteries → Conductance vessels

  • Capillaries → Main site of exchange

Exam Pearl: Arterioles = resistance vessels.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৭) Which layer of adrenal cortex occupies maximum space?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The zona fasciculata is the largest and thickest layer of the adrenal cortex, occupying approximately 75% of the adrenal cortex. It mainly secretes glucocorticoids, especially cortisol.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Zona glomerulosa → Mineralocorticoids → Aldosterone

  • Zona fasciculata → Glucocorticoids → Cortisol

  • Zona reticularis → Androgens

  • Largest layer → Fasciculata

Mnemonic: GFR = Salt, Sugar, Sex

  • Glomerulosa → Salt

  • Fasciculata → Sugar

  • Reticularis → Sex

Exam Pearl: Zona fasciculata occupies the maximum area of adrenal cortex.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৮) Most of the cells of the pars tuberalis are.......?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The pars tuberalis is a part of the adenohypophysis (anterior pituitary) that surrounds the infundibular stalk. Most of its endocrine cells are gonadotrophs, which secrete FSH and LH.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pars tuberalis → predominantly gonadotrophs

  • Gonadotrophs → FSH + LH

  • Pars distalis → major functional part of anterior pituitary

  • Pars intermedia → melanotrophs; rudimentary in adults

Exam Pearl: Pars tuberalis = gonadotroph-rich region.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৯) Mitosis occurs in which layer of epidermis?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Mitosis (cell division) in the epidermis occurs mainly in the stratum basale (stratum germinativum). It contains proliferating keratinocytes/stem cells, which continuously divide and produce new cells that migrate upward through the epidermal layers.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Stratum basale → mitosis + new keratinocytes

  • Stratum spinosum → mainly keratinocyte maturation

  • Stratum granulosum → keratohyalin granules

  • Stratum corneum → dead, keratinized cells

  • Basale is attached to the basement membrane

Exam Pearl: Mitosis in epidermis → Stratum basale.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮০) Which is most commonly involved site for phlebothrombosis?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Phlebothrombosis (deep vein thrombosis) most commonly affects the deep veins of the lower extremities, particularly the calf veins. Venous stasis, endothelial injury, and hypercoagulability (Virchow’s triad) contribute to thrombus formation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common site → Lower limb

  • Common sites → Calf and femoral veins

  • Risk factors → Stasis + endothelial injury + hypercoagulability

  • Major complication → Pulmonary embolism

Exam Pearl: DVT/phlebothrombosis → think lower limb first.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮১) Which Supplies nourishment to retina?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The choroid is a highly vascular layer of the eye that provides oxygen and nutrients to the outer retina, especially the photoreceptors (rods and cones).

The inner retina receives its blood supply mainly from the central retinal artery, while the outer retina is nourished primarily by the choriocapillaris of the choroid.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Choroid → nourishes outer retina

  • Central retinal artery → inner retina

  • Sclera → protective outer layer

  • Cornea → transparent refractive surface

  • Iris → controls pupil size

Exam Pearl: Choroid = vascular supply/nourishment of the outer retina.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮২) Myoepithelial cells aid in the secretory process of which of the following?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Myoepithelial cells are contractile cells located between the secretory epithelial cells and basement membrane of certain glands. Their contraction helps squeeze secretions out of the glandular units.

In the skin, myoepithelial cells are prominent around the secretory portions of eccrine sweat glands and assist in the secretion of sweat.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Myoepithelial cells → Eccrine sweat glands

  • They are contractile

  • Help expel glandular secretions

  • Also found in some mammary and salivary glands

Exam Pearl: Myoepithelial cells aid secretion in eccrine sweat glands.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৩) Sebaceous glands are present in which layer of skin?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Sebaceous glands are located in the dermis, mainly associated with hair follicles. They are generally situated in the reticular layer of the dermis, which is the deeper and thicker portion of the dermis.

They secrete sebum, an oily substance that lubricates and protects the skin and hair.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Sebaceous glands → Reticular dermis

  • Usually associated with → Hair follicles

  • Secretion → Sebum

  • Sebaceous glands are absent from → Palms and soles

Exam Pearl: Sebaceous gland = reticular layer of dermis.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৪) Nissl granules are composed of.....?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Nissl granules (Nissl bodies) are composed mainly of rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) with associated ribosomes. They are abundant in the cell body (soma) and dendrites of neurons and are responsible for extensive protein synthesis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Nissl granules → RER + ribosomes

  • Location → Soma and dendrites

  • Absent from → Axon hillock and axon

  • Function → Protein synthesis

Exam Pearl: Nissl substance = concentrated RER.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৫) What is the type of 1st carpometacarpal joint?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The 1st carpometacarpal (CMC) joint, between the trapezium and base of the 1st metacarpal, is a saddle (sellar) joint.

This joint allows the thumb's important movements, especially flexion, extension, abduction, adduction, and opposition.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • 1st CMC joint → Saddle

  • Bones → Trapezium + 1st metacarpal

  • Major function → Thumb opposition

  • Ellipsoid → Radiocarpal joint

  • Hinge → Interphalangeal joints

  • Pivot → Proximal radioulnar joint

Exam Pearl: Thumb CMC = saddle joint.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৬)  Outer bony Labyrinth is filled with a fluid called.......?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The bony (osseous) labyrinth of the inner ear is filled with perilymph. The membranous labyrinth, which lies within the bony labyrinth, contains endolymph.

Here, options B and C are identical (“Perilymph”), so the question is appropriately invalid/ambiguous as written.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bony labyrinth → Perilymph

  • Membranous labyrinth → Endolymph

  • Perilymph → similar to extracellular fluid

  • Endolymph → rich in K⁺

Exam Pearl: Bony = Perilymph; Membranous = Endolymph.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৭) What is the type of human lens?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The human crystalline lens is a biconvex, transparent, and elastic structure. Its convex shape allows it to refract light and focus images onto the retina. During accommodation, the lens becomes more rounded and convex for near vision.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Human lens → Biconvex

  • Near vision → Lens becomes more convex/thicker

  • Distance vision → Lens becomes flatter

  • Lens is avascular and nourished mainly by aqueous/vitreous fluids

  • Astigmatism → often corrected with a cylindrical lens

Exam Pearl: Crystalline lens = biconvex lens.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৮) Which organelle completes post-translational modifications of proteins?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The Golgi apparatus is the main organelle responsible for post-translational modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins after they are synthesized on ribosomes attached to the rough ER.

Important modifications include glycosylation, sulfation, phosphorylation, and proteolytic processing.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Ribosome → Protein synthesis

  • Rough ER → Protein synthesis + initial folding/modification

  • Golgi apparatus → Further modification + sorting + packaging

  • Smooth ER → Lipid synthesis + detoxification

Exam Pearl: Post-translational modification and protein sorting → Golgi apparatus.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৯) Tetrad formation occurs in which stage of cell division?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Tetrad formation occurs during the pachytene stage of Prophase I of meiosis. During pachytene, homologous chromosomes are fully paired through synapsis, forming bivalents/tetrads, each containing four chromatids. Crossing over also occurs during pachytene.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Leptotene → Chromosomes condense

  • Zygotene → Synapsis begins

  • Pachytene → Tetrad formation + crossing over

  • Diplotene → Chiasmata become visible

  • Diakinesis → Terminalization of chiasmata

Exam Pearl: Pachytene = tetrad + crossing over.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯০) Thunderclap headache is a feature of......?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A thunderclap headache is a sudden, severe headache that reaches maximum intensity within seconds to a minute. It is classically associated with subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), often due to rupture of a berry (saccular) aneurysm.

Other causes can produce thunderclap headache, but in an exam, SAH is the classic association.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Thunderclap headache → SAH

  • SAH → sudden severe “worst headache of life”

  • Common cause → ruptured berry aneurysm

  • Meningitis → headache + fever + neck stiffness, usually not classically thunderclap

Exam Pearl: Sudden “worst headache of life” = think SAH first.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯১) Which of the following Propels sperm?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The flagellum (tail) of the sperm is responsible for propelling sperm forward. It contains an axoneme with a 9+2 arrangement of microtubules, which generates the characteristic wave-like movement.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Sperm movement → Flagellum

  • Flagellum → 9+2 microtubule arrangement

  • Cilia → Move fluid/material over epithelial surfaces

  • Microvilli → Increase surface area

  • Stereocilia → Long, non-motile microvilli-like structures

Exam Pearl: Sperm propulsion = flagellum.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯২) What is the root value of Knee jerk?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The knee jerk (patellar reflex) is mediated mainly by the L2–L4 spinal nerve roots, with L4 being the most important/root predominantly tested. Tapping the patellar tendon stretches the quadriceps muscle spindle, producing contraction of the quadriceps and extension of the knee.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Knee jerk → L2–L4 ⭐

  • Ankle jerk → S1–S2

  • Biceps jerk → C5–C6

  • Triceps jerk → C7–C8

Exam Pearl: Knee jerk = L4 (mainly), tested within L2–L4.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৩) Which one passes through aortic opening?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The aortic opening (aortic hiatus) of the diaphragm is located at approximately T12. It transmits the descending aorta, thoracic duct, and azygos vein.

The vagus nerves pass through the esophageal hiatus (T10), while the phrenic nerves pass through the diaphragm separately. The gastric artery does not pass through the aortic hiatus.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • T8 — Caval opening → IVC

  • T10 — Esophageal hiatus → Esophagus + vagal trunks

  • T12 — Aortic hiatus → Aorta + thoracic duct + azygos vein

Exam Pearl: Aortic hiatus = T12 → aorta + thoracic duct + azygos vein.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৪) Mutation means permanent change in......?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A mutation is a permanent change in the nucleotide sequence of DNA. Mutations can occur spontaneously or be caused by mutagens such as radiation, chemicals, or certain biological agents.

Mutations may involve a single nucleotide (point mutation) or larger changes such as insertions, deletions, duplications, or chromosomal rearrangements.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Mutation → permanent change in DNA

  • Point mutation → change in a single nucleotide/base

  • Germline mutation → can be inherited

  • Somatic mutation → occurs in body cells and is generally not inherited

Exam Pearl: Mutation = permanent alteration of DNA sequence.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৫) Intrinsic pathway is assessed by which of the following?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The intrinsic pathway of coagulation is assessed by the Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (APTT/aPTT). It evaluates factors XII, XI, IX, and VIII, as well as the common pathway factors.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Intrinsic pathway → APTT

  • Extrinsic pathway → PT/INR

  • Common pathway → PT and APTT

  • BT → Platelet function/primary hemostasis

  • CT → Older, less specific test of clotting time

Exam Pearl: Intrinsic = APTT; Extrinsic = PT.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৬) Which controls gallbladder contractility?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Cholecystokinin (CCK) is the principal hormone responsible for gallbladder contraction. It is released from I cells of the duodenum and jejunum in response mainly to fatty acids and amino acids. CCK also promotes relaxation of the sphincter of Oddi, allowing bile to enter the duodenum.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • CCK → Gallbladder contraction ⭐

  • CCK → Relaxes sphincter of Oddi

  • CCK → Stimulates pancreatic enzyme secretion

  • Secretin → Stimulates bicarbonate-rich pancreatic secretion

  • Gastrin → Stimulates gastric acid secretion

Exam Pearl: CCK = contracts the gallbladder and releases bile.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৭) Which is a complication of measles?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Diarrhoea is a common complication of measles, particularly in children. Measles can cause gastrointestinal involvement and may lead to significant fluid and nutritional losses.

Other important complications include otitis media, pneumonia, laryngotracheobronchitis, and encephalitis. A rare late complication is subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), which causes progressive neurological deterioration and dementia-like symptoms years after measles infection.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Measles → Diarrhoea ⭐

  • Common complications → Pneumonia, otitis media, laryngotracheobronchitis

  • Neurological → Encephalitis

  • Late complication → SSPE

Exam Pearl: Measles commonly causes diarrhoea; SSPE is the classic delayed neurological complication.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৮) Which is live attenuated vaccine?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
BCG (Bacillus Calmette–Guérin) is a live attenuated bacterial vaccine derived from Mycobacterium bovis. It is primarily used to provide protection against severe forms of tuberculosis, especially in children.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • BCG → Live attenuated ⭐

  • HBV → Recombinant/subunit vaccine

  • HCV → No licensed vaccine

  • Pertussis → Inactivated whole-cell or acellular components

Exam Pearl: BCG = live attenuated vaccine.

Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৯) Causes of hypopigmentation excludes....?
Final Model Test-03 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
